deepDive.title: AI Just Broke Real Encryption — Banks Need to Pay Attention
deepDive.html:
Overview

Anthropic's Mythos model — purpose-built for scientific research — has discovered genuine vulnerabilities in cryptographic algorithms, cracking a weakened version of AES and breaking the HAWK post-quantum signature scheme. AI-assisted cryptanalysis just moved from theoretical to demonstrable.

The Details

  • Anthropic's Claude Mythos model identified exploitable weaknesses in real cryptographic algorithms, with findings published by Anthropic and validated by external media including The New York Times.
  • Cracked a reduced-round ("weakened") form of AES — the encryption standard underpinning the vast majority of global financial transactions.
  • Broke HAWK, a post-quantum digital signature scheme under active consideration as a candidate for next-generation cryptographic standards.
  • Anthropic framed this as a responsible disclosure and published the methodology openly — making it a reproducible, peer-visible result.
  • The story was picked up by The New York Times, Firstpost, Startup Fortune, and multiple major outlets — this is not a vendor claim.

Why It Matters

Banks rely on AES for everything from ATM transaction encryption to SWIFT messaging and core banking data protection. Production AES-256 wasn't broken here — but the signal is unmistakable: AI can now systematically probe cryptographic algorithms at machine speed and scale. The era of automated cryptanalysis has arrived, and it will only accelerate as models become more capable.

More immediately alarming: HAWK is a post-quantum signature scheme that institutions have been quietly evaluating as a hedge against quantum computing threats. If AI can break next-generation cryptographic candidates before they even reach deployment, the post-quantum migration playbook needs urgent reassessment. CISOs should be running crypto algorithm inventories and stress-testing their roadmaps now — not after a breach forces the issue.

items.tagline: Open-source AI voice model platform for creators and enterprise
items.summary: Fish Audio raised $52M in seed funding, with 8 million users already on its open-source or hosted voice models and $21M in annual recurring revenue — strong traction before a Series A.
items.analysis: **Voice AI with real revenue.** The $21M ARR at seed stage signals genuine product-market fit; for banks exploring AI-powered voice authentication or IVR replacement, Fish Audio's open model approach offers a credible alternative to legacy voice vendors.

items.tagline: Speech-to-speech AI models for natural, real-time voice interaction
items.summary: Founded by ex-AWS scientist Alex Smola, Boson AI is building speech-to-speech models it believes will redefine human-machine voice interaction — competing directly with OpenAI and Meta in the voice AI race.
items.analysis: **Research pedigree with enterprise ambition.** Smola co-developed foundational ML infrastructure at Amazon; Boson's native speech-to-speech approach (no text middleman) is directly relevant to banks evaluating voice interfaces for wealth advisory and contact centres.

items.headline: DBS introduces agentic AI to 350,000 corporate clients
items.summary: DBS Bank has rolled out agentic AI capabilities to its entire corporate client base — 350,000 companies — enabling AI assistants to autonomously handle banking tasks on behalf of clients. This is among the largest external agentic AI deployments at a single financial institution to date.
items.keyPoint: **Scale is the signal.** When Asia's most digitally advanced bank moves agentic AI from internal tooling to 350,000 external clients, it marks a structural shift in how corporate banking relationships will be delivered.

items.headline: HSBC Commits to Proprietary AI in Singapore as Agentic Treasury Goes Mainstream
items.summary: HSBC is doubling down on proprietary AI for treasury operations in Singapore, building in-house models rather than relying on third-party tools, as agentic treasury management begins displacing traditional cash management workflows.
items.keyPoint: **Build vs. buy is being decided now.** HSBC's bet on bespoke treasury AI signals that competitive advantage will increasingly come from internal model development — banks deferring that decision are falling behind.

items.headline: INETCO Launches BullzAI Investigate to Slash Fraud Investigation Times by 99% Using Agentic AI
items.summary: INETCO launched BullzAI Investigate, an agentic AI tool that claims to cut fraud investigation times by 99% by autonomously gathering transaction evidence, cross-referencing patterns, and surfacing conclusions that traditionally take fraud analysts hours.
items.keyPoint: **A 99% time reduction demands real-world validation.** If it holds at production scale, BullzAI could fundamentally change the economics of fraud operations at banks and payment processors — cutting costs or dramatically expanding coverage.

items.headline: Eltropy Takes Agentic AI on the Road Across the Credit Union and Community Banking Industry
items.summary: Eltropy is expanding its agentic AI platform specifically to credit unions and community banks — institutions that typically lack resources to build AI in-house — through a U.S. industry roadshow.
items.keyPoint: **Agentic AI is reaching the long tail.** As purpose-built platforms arrive at smaller institutions, competitive pressure on mid-market banks and credit unions to deploy AI capabilities is intensifying rapidly.

items.headline: Microsoft's new AI model beats Mythos on security benchmark
items.summary: Microsoft's new purpose-built cybersecurity AI model outperforms Anthropic's Mythos on security benchmarks, alongside a new agentic cybersecurity platform that can autonomously detect, investigate, and respond to threats.
items.keyPoint: **Cybersecurity AI is specializing fast.** Banks now have access to purpose-built security models that outperform general frontier models at threat detection — a meaningful upgrade for SOC teams and incident response operations.
